# RAOM safe recovery and watchdog protection

1. Kind: improve. Depends on completed ITM-0007. Extend delivered RAOM without reopening its completed record.
2. Add explicit operator-requested transition from safe mode to normal mode through a system reboot. Accept command only when valid current mode is safe. Reject normal, missing, or invalid mode without changing services or recovery state.
3. Acknowledge repaired reset condition so prior reset evidence cannot immediately trigger safe mode again after recovery or reboot. Preserve reset history. New resets must still trigger safe mode when configured threshold is exceeded. NTP and other decision errors retain configured policy.
4. Persistent acknowledged reset baseline is a proposed mechanism, not approved design. Command interface is `scr-raom switch <mode>`, with `safe` and `normal` targets. Planner must define evidence boundary, persistence, counter discontinuities, and behavior when evidence is unavailable. Do not silently disable threshold or error protection.
5. Fix shipped safe MONIT profile to enable native full watchdog protection for MONIT. MONIT remains sole supervisor of client-defined safe services. Watchdog checks must work in safe mode without requiring intentionally disabled normal services. Client retains safe service inventory ownership; Cloudflare provisioning remains excluded.
6. Preserve verified hardware feeding during mode transition, MONIT stop/start, and watchdog handoff. Full watchdog must activate only after selected MONIT instance is verified. Prevent competing watchdog and keepalive feeders.
7. Both explicit switches persist the requested transition and reboot the system; no live profile switch. Serialize with existing service actions. Distinguish accepted reboot request from verified completion on next boot. Persist required mode/recovery state before requesting reboot. Define interrupted writes, failed reboot requests, boot failures, and retry behavior. Verify selected MONIT and full watchdog after boot. Do not claim the requested mode is running merely because reboot was requested.
8. Reuse RAOM locking, state publication, MONIT validation, native service adapters, shared logging, and root checks. Consume existing scr-resets-monitor evidence interface. Limit any dependency changes to demonstrated recovery needs; no general reset-monitor or watchdog redesign.
9. Deliver updated unified scr-raom Debian package and update src/tools/raom/README.md as part of this item. README must describe final implemented algorithm in Structured English, single scr-raom switch <mode> interface, both reboot-based transitions, persistent safe state, reset acknowledgment, watchdog behavior, NTP caveat, and failure limits. Use dpkg-based installation, upgrade, rollback, and package verification rather than manual payload copies.
10. Acceptance covers source-mode enforcement for both targets of the single switch command, successful normal-to-safe switching, successful recovery through reboot, no retrigger from acknowledged evidence across reboot, retained history, new threshold violations, error policy, safe service supervision, MONIT watchdog protection in both modes, and transition failure behavior.
11. Keep mandatory repository gates and applicable locked disposable-image restoration checks distinct from focused acceptance tests. Preserve original images and historical package evidence. Mark hardware-required; require identified target/image, exact package hash, explicit operation authority, logs, rollback, and developer hardware confirmation before DONE.
12. Out of scope: automatic recovery, permanent threshold bypass, history deletion, client service deployment, Cloudflare, unrelated OS repairs, and unapproved hardware operations. Switch requests reboot instead of changing live service selection.
13. Developer authorized CHN-0002 execution after intake. ITM-0008 is third member and remains at independent planning. Explicit plan, SHOW, and hardware approvals remain required; no device operation authorized.
14. Add explicit operator-requested transition from normal mode to safe mode through a system reboot, without requiring a reset threshold violation. Accept only valid current normal mode. Reject safe, missing, stale, or invalid selection without changing services or recovery state. Apply protected MONIT/watchdog handoff and supervise selected safe services. Manual safe entry must not implicitly acknowledge reset evidence. Persist safe mode across reboots. Only successful explicit switch normal clears safe mode.
15. Expose one command: `scr-raom switch <mode>`. Supported target modes: `safe` and `normal`. `switch normal` accepts only valid current safe mode; `switch safe` accepts only valid current normal mode. Reject unknown targets, malformed arguments, same-mode requests, and missing/stale/invalid selection without changing services or recovery state. The single command performs or rejects the requested transition through shared validation and protected handoff. Do not expose separate recovery or mode-entry commands. Preserve recovery acknowledgment semantics for successful safe-to-normal transitions only.
16. Safe mode is persistent regardless of entry cause: administrator request, reset threshold, or configured error policy. Administrator `scr-raom switch safe` enters safe without threshold evaluation. A reboot from safe mode must select safe regardless of threshold; only successful `scr-raom switch normal` clears persistent safe state. Boots without persistent safe state evaluate ordinary RAOM threshold/readiness/error policy. Threshold observations, if collected during persisted-safe boot, cannot clear or override safe mode. Preserve this behavior across reboot and package upgrade. This supersedes prior proposal to reevaluate manual safe mode into normal on reboot.
17. README acceptance: explain that automatic boot evaluation can wait up to configured NTP_SYNC_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (current default 60 seconds), after separately bounded NTP startup. Synchronization may finish sooner or fail; timeout is not a synchronization guarantee. During wait native networking/logging/NTP run and wd_keepalive feeds hardware timer; full watchdog MONIT checks and MONIT-managed application services start only after selection and verified MONIT startup. Persisted-safe boot needs no NTP-backed threshold decision; document the final implemented path explicitly. Do not confuse timer feeding with MONIT health supervision or historical timeout latency with successful NTP synchronization.
18. Document exact switch arguments, source-mode rejection, reboot side effect, persistent-state semantics, next-boot error policy, and command/result diagnostics. Reconcile architecture/boot diagrams, algorithm, user commands, and watchdog sections with delivered behavior. Preserve current user README edits. Documentation is an owned ITM-0008 implementation deliverable, not a claim that unimplemented commands exist today. Final plan must resolve reset-acknowledgment availability and switch-normal NTP/error semantics without inventing an admin-command prerequisite.
19. Developer approved recovery counter gate: switch normal captures current hardware reset counters without waiting for NTP and durably saves acknowledgment before requesting reboot. If counters cannot be read or the recovery baseline cannot be saved, return failure, retain safe mode, and refuse reboot. No NTP synchronization prerequisite is added to the admin command. Subsequent boot retains configured NTP/error policy; acknowledgment excludes old reset evidence, not new faults.
20. Exclude the reboot caused by an explicit mode switch from threshold counting when the comparable BMC reset-counter increase associated with that request is exactly 1. If the increase is greater than 1, do not exempt that increase; retain the full observed increase as eligible reset evidence under existing time-window and error rules. This exception applies only to an identified requested mode-switch reboot, not arbitrary subsequent reboots. Preserve raw counters and reset history. Do not infer an exact increment from unavailable evidence, counter decrease, or changed controller identity. Revise design, acceptance, and documentation accordingly. Supersedes proposed unconditional counting of requested reboots. Safe-mode persistence remains unchanged.

# RAOM safe recovery and watchdog protection

1. Kind: improve. Depends on completed ITM-0007. Extend delivered RAOM without reopening its completed record.
2. Add explicit operator-requested transition from safe mode to normal mode through a system reboot. Accept command only when valid current mode is safe. Reject normal, missing, or invalid mode without changing services or recovery state.
3. Acknowledge repaired reset condition so prior reset evidence cannot immediately trigger safe mode again after recovery or reboot. Preserve reset history. New resets must still trigger safe mode when configured threshold is exceeded. NTP and other decision errors retain configured policy.
4. Persistent acknowledged reset baseline is a proposed mechanism, not approved design. Command interface is `scr-raom switch <mode>`, with `safe` and `normal` targets. Planner must define evidence boundary, persistence, counter discontinuities, and behavior when evidence is unavailable. Do not silently disable threshold or error protection.
5. Fix shipped safe MONIT profile to enable native full watchdog protection for MONIT. MONIT remains sole supervisor of client-defined safe services. Watchdog checks must work in safe mode without requiring intentionally disabled normal services. Client retains safe service inventory ownership; Cloudflare provisioning remains excluded.
6. Preserve verified hardware feeding during mode transition, MONIT stop/start, and watchdog handoff. Full watchdog must activate only after selected MONIT instance is verified. Prevent competing watchdog and keepalive feeders.
7. Both explicit switches persist the requested transition and reboot the system; no live profile switch. Serialize with existing service actions. Distinguish accepted reboot request from verified completion on next boot. Persist required mode/recovery state before requesting reboot. Define interrupted writes, failed reboot requests, boot failures, and retry behavior. Verify selected MONIT and full watchdog after boot. Do not claim the requested mode is running merely because reboot was requested.
8. Reuse RAOM locking, state publication, MONIT validation, native service adapters, shared logging, and root checks. Consume existing scr-resets-monitor evidence interface. Limit any dependency changes to demonstrated recovery needs; no general reset-monitor or watchdog redesign.
9. Deliver updated unified scr-raom Debian package and update src/tools/raom/README.md as part of this item. README must describe final implemented algorithm in Structured English, single scr-raom switch <mode> interface, both reboot-based transitions, persistent safe state, reset acknowledgment, watchdog behavior, NTP caveat, and failure limits. Use dpkg-based installation, upgrade, rollback, and package verification rather than manual payload copies.
10. Acceptance covers source-mode enforcement for both targets of the single switch command, successful normal-to-safe switching, successful recovery through reboot, no retrigger from acknowledged evidence across reboot, retained history, new threshold violations, error policy, safe service supervision, MONIT watchdog protection in both modes, and transition failure behavior.
11. Keep mandatory repository gates and applicable locked disposable-image restoration checks distinct from focused acceptance tests. Preserve original images and historical package evidence. Mark hardware-required; require identified target/image, exact package hash, explicit operation authority, logs, rollback, and developer hardware confirmation before DONE.
12. Out of scope: automatic recovery, permanent threshold bypass, history deletion, client service deployment, Cloudflare, unrelated OS repairs, and unapproved hardware operations. Switch requests reboot instead of changing live service selection.
13. Developer authorized CHN-0002 execution after intake. ITM-0008 is third member and remains at independent planning. Explicit plan, SHOW, and hardware approvals remain required; no device operation authorized.
14. Add explicit operator-requested transition from normal mode to safe mode through a system reboot, without requiring a reset threshold violation. Accept only valid current normal mode. Reject safe, missing, stale, or invalid selection without changing services or recovery state. Apply protected MONIT/watchdog handoff and supervise selected safe services. Manual safe entry must not implicitly acknowledge reset evidence. Persist safe mode across reboots. Only successful explicit switch normal clears safe mode.
15. Expose one command: `scr-raom switch <mode>`. Supported target modes: `safe` and `normal`. `switch normal` accepts only valid current safe mode; `switch safe` accepts only valid current normal mode. Reject unknown targets, malformed arguments, same-mode requests, and missing/stale/invalid selection without changing services or recovery state. The single command performs or rejects the requested transition through shared validation and protected handoff. Do not expose separate recovery or mode-entry commands. Preserve recovery acknowledgment semantics for successful safe-to-normal transitions only.
16. Safe mode is persistent regardless of entry cause: administrator request, reset threshold, or configured error policy. Administrator `scr-raom switch safe` enters safe without threshold evaluation. A reboot from safe mode must select safe regardless of threshold; only successful `scr-raom switch normal` clears persistent safe state. Boots without persistent safe state evaluate ordinary RAOM threshold/readiness/error policy. Threshold observations, if collected during persisted-safe boot, cannot clear or override safe mode. Preserve this behavior across reboot and package upgrade. This supersedes prior proposal to reevaluate manual safe mode into normal on reboot.
17. README acceptance: explain that automatic boot evaluation can wait up to configured NTP_SYNC_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (current default 60 seconds), after separately bounded NTP startup. Synchronization may finish sooner or fail; timeout is not a synchronization guarantee. During wait native networking/logging/NTP run and wd_keepalive feeds hardware timer; full watchdog MONIT checks and MONIT-managed application services start only after selection and verified MONIT startup. Persisted-safe boot needs no NTP-backed threshold decision; document the final implemented path explicitly. Do not confuse timer feeding with MONIT health supervision or historical timeout latency with successful NTP synchronization.
18. Document exact switch arguments, source-mode rejection, reboot side effect, persistent-state semantics, next-boot error policy, and command/result diagnostics. Reconcile architecture/boot diagrams, algorithm, user commands, and watchdog sections with delivered behavior. Preserve current user README edits. Documentation is an owned ITM-0008 implementation deliverable, not a claim that unimplemented commands exist today. Final plan must resolve reset-acknowledgment availability and switch-normal NTP/error semantics without inventing an admin-command prerequisite.
19. Developer approved recovery counter gate: switch normal captures current hardware reset counters without waiting for NTP and durably saves acknowledgment before requesting reboot. If counters cannot be read or the recovery baseline cannot be saved, return failure, retain safe mode, and refuse reboot. No NTP synchronization prerequisite is added to the admin command. Subsequent boot retains configured NTP/error policy; acknowledgment excludes old reset evidence, not new faults.
